candidate.answerReason: The equal parallel chords lie on opposite sides of the center, each 4 inches away. Each outer cap has area \(64\pi/3-16\sqrt3\); subtracting both from the circle gives \(32\sqrt3+64\pi/3\).

methods.label: Subtract the two outer caps
methods.explanation:
The region between the chords is the whole circle with two outer caps removed. We can find each cap by subtracting a triangle from a sector.

Let \(O\) be the center. Perpendiculars from \(O\) bisect the equal chords. The resulting right triangles have equal hypotenuses and equal half-chords, so the Pythagorean theorem gives equal distances from \(O\) to the chords. Since the distinct chords are parallel, they must lie on opposite sides of \(O\); otherwise equal distances would put them on the same line. Their separation is \(8\), so each chord is \(4\) inches from \(O\).

Choose one chord \(AB\), and let \(H\) be its midpoint. Then
\[
AH=\sqrt{8^2-4^2}=4\sqrt3,
\qquad AB=8\sqrt3.
\]
To find the central angle, reflect \(O\) across \(AB\) to \(O'\). Reflection preserves distances from \(A\), so
\[
OO'=2OH=8,\qquad AO'=AO=8.
\]
Thus \(AOO'\) is equilateral, giving \(\angle AOH=60^\circ\). The perpendicular through the center also bisects \(\angle AOB\), so \(\angle AOB=120^\circ\).

Triangle \(OAB\) has area
\[
\frac12(8\sqrt3)(4)=16\sqrt3.
\]
Therefore the outer cap bounded by \(AB\) has area
\[
\frac{120}{360}\pi(8^2)-16\sqrt3
=\frac{64\pi}{3}-16\sqrt3.
\]
The other cap has the same area, and the two caps are disjoint. Subtracting them from the circle gives
\[
64\pi-2\left(\frac{64\pi}{3}-16\sqrt3\right)
=\boxed{32\sqrt3+\frac{64\pi}{3}}.
\]
Since \(64/3=21\frac13\), this is choice B, in square inches.
